text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users can get better results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are very useful for tasks like writing, translating and answering questions. However, they also have limits. They sometimes make mistakes or give false information, and their knowledge stops at a certain date. For these reasons, it is always wise to check their answers carefully.
